question.problem: Which curve is defined by the equation $5{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}=12?$

current_example.problem: Which curve is defined by the equation $6x_1^2+8x_1x_2-9x_2^2= 70?$
current_example.worked_solution:
Consider the quadratic form $Q(\mathbf{x})=6x_1^2+8x_1x_2-9x_2^2.$ To  determine the curve defined by the given equation, we reduce $Q(\mathbf{x})$ to its canonical (diagonal) form.

First, we write down the matrix of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ which is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/9068501a5c49ec0dc49ec786cfcfaab618ac9797c1a930e3657b7f46de9c4367.svg)

Next, we find the eigenvalues of $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}6-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & -9-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda -70 & =0 \\ \lambda  & =7,\,-10\end{aligned}
$$

So, our quadratic form can be reduced to $7y_1^2 -10 y_2^2.$  

In the new variables, the curve has the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}7{y}_{1}^{2}-10{y}_{2}^{2} & =70 \\ \frac{{y}_{1}^{2}}{10}-\frac{{y}_{2}^{2}}{7} & =1 \\ \frac{{y}_{1}^{2}}{(\sqrt{10})^{2}}-\frac{{y}_{2}^{2}}{(\sqrt{7})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This is a hyperbola with semiaxes $\sqrt{10}$ and $\sqrt{7}.$
